attributes.title: Level 3

subgroups.name: Discover

steps.text: Watch this video to learn about how to create block statements in your projects by adding code inside of an event or loop.

questions.hint: What term can you use to describe the code inside of another line of code?
questions.title: [Select one] A  ______________ is a chunk of indented lines of code that will run inside of another line of code.
questions.correctResponse: Remember, block statements are indented lines of code that will run inside of another line of code, such as an event or loop.

questions.hint: What symbols always surround a block statement?
questions.title: [Select one] Block statements are not found within the curly brackets { } of another line of code.
questions.correctResponse: In order for the code to run correctly, block statements need to be contained within curly brackets { }. These serve the same purpose as containers did in the blocks editor!

questions.hint: What might you do when you want to move code from one event or loop into another?
questions.title: [Select one] Cutting and pasting lines of code from one block statement into another is like:

answers.text: Dragging a block of code from the menu into the editor.
Toggling between the blocks and JavaScript editors to read code.
Doing an arts and crafts project.
Dragging a code block from one container and dropping it into another.

questions.correctResponse: Because you can’t move lines of code as easily in JavaScript as you could in blocks, cutting and pasting code allows you to more quickly change where code is placed in the editor.

questions.hint: What will the code inside of the controller.A event do?
questions.title: [Select one] Based on the code, what will happen when the A button is pressed?

answers.text: A new sprite will be created.
The confetti screen effect will start and the magicWand sound will play.
The blizzard screen effect will start and the baDing sound will play.

questions.correctResponse: The block statement for the controller.A event is contained within its curly brackets { }: blizzard.startScreenEffect and music.play(music.melodyPlayable(music.baDing), music.PlaybackMode.UntilDone).

subgroups.title: Block Statements!
subgroups.introduction: Watch this video to learn about how to create block statements in your projects by adding code inside of an event or loop.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 3 of Blue Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about block statements. In JavaScript, instead of adding code into different containers, you’ll add block statements inside curly brackets { } of an event or a loop. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 3:

badges.title: Thinking Inside the Block
badges.description: Use block statements inside curly brackets { } to add code inside of events and loops.

badges.title: Projectile Manager
badges.description: Create a  projectile in JavaScript.

badges.title: Game On (Update Interval)
badges.description: Use a game update loop in JavaScript.

badges.title: About Yay High
badges.description: Use the screen object’s height property instead of a number.

badges.title: Framing the Discussion
badges.description: Use setDialogFrame to design a custom text box.

badges.title: Settle the Score
badges.description: Set the score in JavaScript.

badges.title: Cute as a Button
badges.description: Use a button event in JavaScript.
